A1.justification: Both complete 18-page PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching reorganized and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original virtual try-on experiments, synthetic-data and classifier ablations, qualitative results, and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative and qualitative evaluation on WVTON.

M1.justification: The human-to-garment model, synthetic-data filtering and augmentation, weakly supervised classifier, error-aware bridge, classifier guidance, and expert denoisers remain unchanged. Rewritten explanations and updated diagram labels do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix E adds an out-of-domain, in-the-wild WVTON test. This extends evaluation coverage while retaining the same virtual try-on task, original benchmarks, and synthetic training datasets.

E2.justification: The augmentation comparison no longer reports CAT-DM +W(H2G-UH) and Stable-VTON +W(H2G-UH), present in v1 Table 3(a). Main benchmark comparators remain unchanged; GP-GAN/GP-VTON and Stable-VTON/StableVITON naming corrections do not introduce new methods.

E3.justification: The added WVTON evaluation specifies unpaired testing with image backgrounds removed (v2 Table 8 and Appendix E). Existing benchmark splits, evaluation resolution, metrics, and sampling-step settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an out-of-domain generalization test and accompanying visual example. It removes the reported warped-garment controls for CAT-DM and StableVITON, while retaining the corresponding EARSB control and the existing noise-schedule, classifier, and initial-image-quality analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The user-study specification of 100 image pairs with at least three workers per image is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 Table 8 newly reports WVTON FID/KID values of 131.76/2.10 for Stable-VTON, 127.15/1.67 for EARSB(SD), and 120.29/1.18 with H2G-UH; Figure 12 adds a qualitative example. Main benchmark and user-study values are unchanged. Two warped-garment control rows are omitted, while several existing results are merely redisplayed.

T1.justification: The task definition, losses, bridge formulation, sampling equations, and guidance equations retain the same mathematical content. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: synthetic training pairs and spatially error-aware refinement. The headline claims about the two original benchmarks and average 59% user preference are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix E interprets the new WVTON results as evidence of generalization beyond the original benchmarks. Existing limitations concerning synthetic texture deformation and dependence on initial-image quality are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository hyperlink in the abstract and discloses 102.6M model parameters in Table 6. The table's other training settings largely consolidate information already present in v1 Appendix A.

R1.justification: v2 adds Qraitem et al.'s 'From Fake to Real' as support for synthetic pretraining followed by real-data finetuning. The broader related-work discussion and research positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 folds the standalone task definition into the synthetic-data section, separates experimental setup from results, and edits method and experiment prose. It also standardizes baseline names, adds acknowledgments, and shortens the ethics discussion while preserving the overall narrative.

P2.justification: v2 reorganizes Table 1, splits v1 Table 3 into Tables 3–5, and adds implementation Table 6 and WVTON Table 8/Figure 12. Appendix displays move and are renumbered; existing figures are largely retained with limited label and formatting updates.

improvement.justification: The WVTON evaluation adds useful, limited evidence of generalization, while the code hyperlink, parameter disclosure, and reorganized tables improve reproducibility information and readability. Removing two warped-garment controls narrows the ablation evidence somewhat, but the net improvement is modestly positive; the central method and main results remain unchanged.
